topics.label: Introduction and Learning Objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening administrative framing, course context, and learning objectives for the lecture on cancer causes.

topics.label: Cancer Etiology: Intrinsic Mutations, Environmental Exposures, and Epidemiology
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explore the fundamental origins of cancer by evaluating the interplay between intrinsic mutational processes, environmental exposures, and global epidemiological patterns.

topics.label: Infectious Pathogens and Burkitt Lymphoma Pathogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how biological agents such as bacteria, parasites, and viruses contribute to malignancy, using Burkitt lymphoma as a detailed case study.

topics.label: Chemical and Physical Mutagens: Metabolic Activation and DNA Damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine how physical radiation and chemical carcinogens induce direct DNA damage or require xenobiotic metabolism to form mutagenic DNA adducts.

topics.label: Tumor Promotion, Chronic Inflammation, and Two-Stage Carcinogenesis
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics differentiate tumor promoters from initiators, demonstrating how non-mutagenic exposures drive clonal outgrowth through chronic inflammation and intracellular signaling.

topics.label: Host Developmental Timing, Cellular Susceptibility, and Mechanistic Summary
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics illustrate how tissue developmental stage and proliferative state govern susceptibility to carcinogens, concluding with a synthesis of the mechanisms of carcinogenesis.

topics.label: Methodologies for Detecting and Proving Carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro experimental approaches used to determine carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic risk.

topics.label: Lecture Conclusion and Risk-Benefit Analysis
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, summarizing environmental risk factors and the everyday balance of risk versus benefit.
